brief: Something to keep my sewing supplies tidy.

requirements.requirement: Keep sewing supplies tidy: separate storage for small and larger items
requirements.evidence: There are 3 full-depth bins: bin:0,0,0 has 3 compartments, bin:1,0,0 has 2 and bin:0,1,0 is open. The notch tray notch:0#-1,1#notch0 adds 3 more small compartments, so different supplies stay apart.
capOpenFaces added 10 solid end caps and lockJoints added 3 joint bolts. check_build passed with no rule errors, and the collision check came back clear.
The prop library has no sewing items, so the stand-ins are a tape measure, a marker and a pen.

finish.summary:
I built a small three-cell organiser for sewing supplies. Three full bases sit in a triangle, and each holds a different drop-in bin:
- a 3-compartment bin at (0,0) for small things like pins, buttons and bobbins
- a 2-compartment bin at (1,0) for thread and notions
- an open full-depth bin at (0,1) for scissors and bigger tools

A 3-compartment notch tray sits in the outside corner between two of the bases for needles and small bits. All open faces have solid end caps, and the joints are bolted so the cells don't slide apart. That's 17 parts, about 1,786 g of filament and roughly 40 hours of printing. The build check passed with no rule errors, and the collision check came back clear.

The prop library has no sewing items, so I used the closest ones I could find:
- a tape measure in the open bin
- a marker standing in the 3-compartment bin, for marking fabric
- a pen in the notch tray

A pencil and a ruler wouldn't place. Tweezers did place but sat out of sight below the rim, so I took them out.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
